title: ARI-RQGM UtilityPolicyCandidate
description: One proposed successor utility policy (docs/plans/ari_rqgm/14 §6.2, owned by Task 14). Mirrors prompt_candidate and rides the SAME prompt-evolution log — no new store. The envelope is the mandatory common one (rqgm_defs.schema.json): its author is the POLICY_MUTATOR, not the policy, because a candidate is a proposal BY a component — which is why component_id / role / prompt_hash name the proposer while the proposed policy rides `policy` (by value) + `policy_hash`. `policy` is the §6.1 body: hash12(canonical_json(policy)) IS policy_hash IS the utility_policy_hash the candidate would freeze if adopted — one value, three names, zero new hashing. Legality (closed value spaces + axis-weight bounds) is NOT expressed here: it is frozen code in ari.rqgm.kernel_rules.UTILITY_POLICY_RULES, inside constitution_hash, and enforced by CK-UTL-001..008 before a candidate can ever score a node. rationale cites ABSTRACT evidence only — never raw attack text. created_at is wall-clock metadata, never hashed (P2). Additive-only evolution.

prompt_hash.description: The PROPOSER's own template hash (the policy_mutator meta-prompt) — the envelope names the author, not the proposal. May be empty when the template is unresolvable (best-effort: a missing template never costs a boundary its candidate).

role.description: The AUTHOR's role: policy_mutator. The TARGET role (utility_policy) is implied by record_type.

policy.description: The §6.1 policy body. The file/record never contains utility_policy_hash itself: the hash is OF the body, and capture_utility_policy re-appends it to the returned dict.
